## Details

<a id="Q-001"></a>
### Q-001

Where do the people and organisation data come from: employees (including gender and service start date for seniority), the organisational structure (country, city, office, unit, department), each employee's Line Manager and each project's members and Project Manager? Options: (a) maintained in this system by Admin/HR; (b) imported or synchronised from existing HR / project systems (which ones?); (c) a mix (say which data comes from where).

**Reason:** The URS needs these data for routing (§4.2), eligibility and entitlements (§4.4, §4.5) and access and reporting scope (§4.8), but names only the card scanner system as an integration and gives no source for them.

**Impact if unanswered:** The system boundary, the integrations, the Admin/HR functions and the data model of employees and organisation cannot be defined; the overview would have to guess the scope.

**Blocking:** True

**Related:**

- [REQ-006](requirements.view.md#REQ-006) Confirm or deny a leave request
- [REQ-008](requirements.view.md#REQ-008) Approve or reject a confirmed leave request
- [REQ-017](requirements.view.md#REQ-017) Configure leave type eligibility rules
- [REQ-023](requirements.view.md#REQ-023) Support a multinational organisational structure
- [REQ-027](requirements.view.md#REQ-027) Role-based access rights

**Answer source:** meeting-minutes/MoM 01 Oct 2026.docx

**Answer:** "They are imported from existing HR systems." (option b). The minutes do not name the HR systems, the interface or the import frequency: follow-up question Q-030.

<a id="Q-002"></a>
### Q-002

Who confirms a leave request when the employee belongs to several projects (several Project Managers) or to no project? Options: (a) every Project Manager of the projects the leave dates affect; (b) any one of them; (c) a designated primary Project Manager; (d) with no project, the request goes straight to the Line Manager.

**Reason:** §4.2 assumes one Project Manager per employee; the URS does not say how confirmation is routed otherwise.

**Impact if unanswered:** The core confirmation path and the employee-project relationship in the data model would be guessed.

**Blocking:** True

**Related:**

- [REQ-006](requirements.view.md#REQ-006) Confirm or deny a leave request
- [REQ-007](requirements.view.md#REQ-007) Auto-confirm a Project Manager's own leave request
- [REQ-020](requirements.view.md#REQ-020) Action dashboards for Project Managers and Line Managers

**Answer source:** meeting-minutes/MoM 01 Oct 2026.docx

**Answer:** "The employee can choose the PM from their assigned projects." This settles the several-projects case: the employee chooses which Project Manager confirms (ASM-014). The minutes do not answer the no-project case: follow-up question Q-031.

<a id="Q-003"></a>
### Q-003

What happens to a leave request that is not confirmed or not approved by the end of the calendar month of its leave start date? Options: (a) it stays pending and can still be acted on; (b) it expires or is cancelled automatically; (c) it is rejected automatically; (d) it is approved automatically; (e) it is escalated (to whom?). And how does the rule apply to leave that spans two months, or to a past-date request submitted on the last day of the month?

**Reason:** §4.2 and §6 require review and approval within the calendar month of the leave start date but do not say what the system does when the deadline passes.

**Impact if unanswered:** The request lifecycle (statuses and transitions) and any month-end scheduled job cannot be specified.

**Blocking:** True

**Related:**

- [REQ-009](requirements.view.md#REQ-009) Complete review and approval within the leave start month
- [REQ-006](requirements.view.md#REQ-006) Confirm or deny a leave request
- [REQ-008](requirements.view.md#REQ-008) Approve or reject a confirmed leave request
- [REQ-001](requirements.view.md#REQ-001) Submit leave request

**Answer source:** meeting-minutes/MoM 01 Oct 2026.docx

**Answer:** Outcome at the deadline: "It's cancelled" (option b). Leave spanning two months and past-date requests on the last day of the month: "As long as the leave duration requested is not from the previous month of current month, it is valid." The minutes do not say who cancels (ASM-012) or when exactly the cut-off is (Q-034), nor how a period that straddles the previous and the current month is handled (ASM-013).

<a id="Q-004"></a>
### Q-004

How is a policy-violating leave request reviewed? (1) Who performs the "manual review": the normal Project Manager then Line Manager steps with the violation highlighted, or an additional review (e.g. by HR)? (2) Which violations are allowed through (e.g. exceeding the remaining entitlement, a leave type the employee is not eligible for, a missing required document)? (3) If approved, what happens to the excess (negative balance, converted to unpaid leave, other)?

**Reason:** §3 and §4.1 allow submission despite a policy violation "subject to review" without saying who reviews, which violations qualify or how an approved violation is accounted for.

**Impact if unanswered:** The review workflow could gain an extra actor and step, and the entitlement accounting rules would be guessed.

**Blocking:** True

**Related:**

- [REQ-002](requirements.view.md#REQ-002) Validate leave requests against leave policy
- [REQ-003](requirements.view.md#REQ-003) Accept policy-violating leave requests for manual review
- [REQ-004](requirements.view.md#REQ-004) Attach required supporting documents to a leave request

**Answer source:** meeting-minutes/MoM 01 Oct 2026.docx

**Answer:** (1) "Who reviews: the line manager." (2) "Leave exceed entitlement is allowed." (3) "If approved, what happens to the excess: The balance stay at 0." Not answered: whether the Project Manager still confirms first (ASM-011), whether other violations (ineligible leave type, missing document) are allowed (Q-032), and whether the excess days are recorded anywhere (Q-033).

### Q-023

What are the measurable performance targets: the peak number of concurrent users, and the response time expected for submitting a request and loading dashboards (e.g. 95% of requests within N seconds) at that load?

**Reason:** §4.8 and §5 ask for scale to 33,000 users and concurrent submissions "without delay" without a measurable target.

**Impact if unanswered:** The performance and scalability NFRs cannot be tested.

**Blocking:** False

**Related:**

- [REQ-028](requirements.view.md#REQ-028) Scale to 33,000 users
- [REQ-029](requirements.view.md#REQ-029) Handle concurrent submissions without delay

<a id="Q-024"></a>
### Q-024

What availability and recovery targets apply (e.g. monthly availability %, support hours across time zones, maximum data loss and recovery time after a failure)?

**Reason:** §4.8 asks for reliability under heavy usage without a target.

**Impact if unanswered:** The reliability NFR cannot be tested and the hosting design has no target.

**Blocking:** False

**Related:**

- [REQ-030](requirements.view.md#REQ-030) Reliable under heavy usage

### Q-025

Which languages are required, and at go-live or later? Should dates, times and time zones follow each office's locale?

**Reason:** §6 says the system should be localised (multi-language) "if needed".

**Impact if unanswered:** The internationalisation NFR has no measurable criteria.

**Blocking:** False

**Related:**

- [REQ-031](requirements.view.md#REQ-031) Multi-language localisation

<a id="Q-026"></a>
### Q-026

Which browsers (and versions) and devices must be supported (phones, tablets, desktop)? Is a native mobile app out of scope?

**Reason:** §5 says web-based and mobile-responsive without naming browsers or devices.

**Impact if unanswered:** The platform NFR cannot be tested.

**Blocking:** False

**Related:**

- [REQ-025](requirements.view.md#REQ-025) Web-based and mobile-responsive

<a id="Q-027"></a>
### Q-027

Uploaded documents such as hospital certificates contain personal health data. Which data-protection rules apply (e.g. GDPR or local laws), who may view the documents, how long are they kept, and which file types and sizes are accepted?

**Reason:** §4.5 requires document uploads but the URS has no safety, privacy or retention requirement.

**Impact if unanswered:** The Safety NFRs and the document-handling rules would be missing.

**Blocking:** False

**Related:**

- [REQ-004](requirements.view.md#REQ-004) Attach required supporting documents to a leave request
- [REQ-018](requirements.view.md#REQ-018) Configure required documentation per leave type

<a id="Q-028"></a>
### Q-028

The URS gives no MoSCoW priority for most requirements (§4.1 – §4.4 use "can" or no modal verb). Please confirm the priority of each requirement, in particular whether submission, confirmation and approval are must-haves.

**Reason:** Priorities were derived from "must" (HIGH) and "should" (MEDIUM); requirements without either are MEDIUM by default.

**Impact if unanswered:** Backlog planning would rely on default priorities.

**Blocking:** False

**Related:**

- [REQ-001](requirements.view.md#REQ-001) Submit leave request
- [REQ-006](requirements.view.md#REQ-006) Confirm or deny a leave request
- [REQ-008](requirements.view.md#REQ-008) Approve or reject a confirmed leave request

### Q-030

The minutes (Q-001) say people and organisation data are imported from existing HR systems. Which HR system or systems provide them, through which interface (API, database view, file export) and how often (real time, daily, on demand)? Please also confirm that project assignments and each project's Project Manager come from these HR systems too, and not from a separate project system.

**Reason:** The minutes settle that the data are imported, but not from which systems, how or how often. Project assignments often live outside HR systems.

**Blocking:** False

<a id="Q-031"></a>
### Q-031

Who confirms a leave request when the employee is assigned to no project? Options: (a) the confirmation step is skipped and the request goes straight to the Line Manager; (b) the Line Manager both confirms and approves; (c) another role confirms (which one?); (d) the case cannot occur, because every employee is always assigned to at least one project.

**Reason:** The minutes answer the several-projects part of Q-002 (the employee chooses the PM from their assigned projects) but not the no-project part.

**Impact if unanswered:** A core path of the review workflow (and whether a request can skip confirmation) would be guessed.

**Blocking:** True

The minutes say exceeding the remaining entitlement is allowed and is reviewed by the Line Manager. ### Q-033

When a request that exceeds the remaining entitlement is approved, the balance stays at 0. Are the excess days recorded anywhere (for example shown as over-entitlement or unpaid days in the reports, or passed on for payroll), or are they simply not counted?

**Reason:** The minutes say the balance stays at 0 but not what becomes of the days above the entitlement.

**Impact if unanswered:** The entitlement accounting and the leave statistics could lose or misreport the excess days.

**Blocking:** False

<a id="Q-034"></a>
### Q-034

Requests not confirmed and approved by the end of the leave start month are cancelled. When exactly is the cut-off: the end of the last day of the month in each office's local time zone, or in one company time zone? Is there any grace period, for example for a past-date request submitted on the last day of the month, which would otherwise be cancelled the same day unless both the Project Manager and the Line Manager act on it?

**Reason:** The minutes state the outcome (cancellation) but not the exact cut-off in a company spread over several countries and time zones.

**Impact if unanswered:** The timing of the month-end cancellation job would be guessed, and late-month requests may be cancelled unexpectedly.

**Blocking:** False

**Related:**

Options: (a) it stays pending and can still be acted on; (b) it expires or is cancelled automatically; (c) it is rejected automatically; (d) it is approved automatically; (e) it is escalated (to whom?). And how does the rule apply to leave that spans two months, or to a past-date request submitted on the last day of the month?

<a id="Q-035"></a>
### Q-035

Leave can be taken in half days (morning / afternoon). How does the weekly attendance check (a day is off work with no check-in or with less than 4 hours of presence) treat a day with a half-day leave? For example, if an employee has a half-day leave and less than 4 hours of presence, is the day reported as off work with a valid leave request, as off work without a leave request, or not reported at all?

**Reason:** The URS's 4-hour rule (§4.3) was written without half-day leave, which the minutes now introduce.

**Impact if unanswered:** The weekly notification could wrongly report half-day leave as absence without leave, or hide real absences.

**Blocking:** False

**Related:**

- [REQ-011](requirements.view.md#REQ-011) Determine off-work days from attendance data
- [REQ-012](requirements.view.md#REQ-012) Send weekly attendance notification
- [REQ-001](requirements.view.md#REQ-001) Submit leave request
